title: Swimming and keeping fit
summary: He loves swimming and taught judo and swimming in the army.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: You don't have to have too many regrets about having a vacation in June if you have one.
I'm frankly looking forward to it because I love to swim. I'm a swimmer, I love to swim. As a matter of fact, in the army down in Florida, I taught Judo and swimming.
Yes. Part of my duties so to speak. Had to go to school for the Judo thing. But swimming, I've always been a fairly good swimmer. Fairly good athlete all my life. Fortunately.
Well you look in marvellous condition. You really do. (LAUGHTER).
Do you have a pool out in Merrick?
The pool's there and I just, I'm only five minutes from the ocean.
Jones Beach. And they have an indoor pool down in Belmore that I do a little swimming there a couple of times a week. Try to keep in shape a little.
George Kleinsinger, the composer, is here in this hotel and he goes across the street to the YMCA to swim every single day of his life.

No matter what the weather is outside. I don't care how cold it is, George swims. (LAUGHTER). And swims the length of the pool and back. I don't know how many times he does that, but he does it. (LAUGHTER).
